@graph.owl:versionInfo: 2026.10-alpha.1 (alpha pre-release, 2026-10-03): published for discussion, not for citation; terms, records and URIs may change or be withdrawn until the first full release
@graph.rdfs:comment: Terms HECTOR adds to Linked Art (CIDOC-CRM) for historical commodities, units of measure and customs rates. Term documentation lives here rather than in the JSON-LD context, which may only define terms. Namespace and URI policy: https://github.com/ihr-digital/hector/blob/main/docs/uri-policy.md
True when a record is a worked example of HECTOR's shape rather than curated data. Its values are chosen to show the structure and must not be cited.
A phonetic transcription (IPA) of a Name, used to match variant spellings across sources.
A historical word or phrase for a unit or commodity, where a full Name record is not warranted.
A place of origin or provenance associated with a commodity, or with a qualifier of one (Normandy, in Normandy canvas).
The simpler commodities a compound commodity is composed of. Also published by the London Customs Accounts glossary.

The number of times a commodity is attested in the London Customs Accounts corpus, as counted by that project's tagger (LCA docs/data/concept_attestation.json) when the record was exported; for a unit, the number of corpus spans the tagger typed as that unit (`unit` or `commodity-unit`).

The dimension a unit measures (mass, length, volume, count, package), given as a HECTOR unit dimension (unit/dimension/<dim>). May hold more than one value: a cask or a sack is both a measure and a package. A property, not part of the unit's URI: units are unit/<slug> (D7, 29 Sep 2026).
The number of grams in one of this unit, as an xsd:decimal. State in the unit's description which definition of the unit the figure follows.

A quantity (a Linked Art Dimension: value and unit) that one of this unit is defined as or equal to, according to the source cited on the Dimension. Where sources disagree, each reading is a separate Dimension with its own source; a doubtful one says so in its note. Commodity-specific contents (a bale of cumin holds 3 cwt) are not definitions. Adopted 29 Sep 2026 (D7).
A customs rate: the valuation or charge a Book of Rates sets on a quantity of a commodity for a period.
Links a commodity to a Rate set on it.

A qualifier the source attaches to the goods a Rate is set on (origin, colour, quality, state, size), so that the rate applies to the commodity so qualified: 'Saffron of beyownd the se' is saffron, qualified as from overseas. Named in its modern form where the words are a spelling in the London Customs Accounts qualifier list, with its AAT concept (equivalent) or place (originPlace); otherwise in the source's words, classified as an attested variant.
The MonetaryAmount of a Rate.
The quantity (a Linked Art Dimension: value and unit) that a Rate's amount is charged on.

The exact value of a pre-decimal sterling amount in pence, as an xsd:decimal (a halfpenny is 0.5, a farthing 0.25). Pounds and shillings do not divide exactly into decimal pounds, so pence is the unit of record.
The amount as written in pounds, shillings and pence, for display.
The year from which a Rate or a Name is attested or in force (xsd:gYear).
The last year in which a Rate or a Name is attested or in force (xsd:gYear).
The source (for example a Book of Rates) that a Name or a Rate is taken from.
The text of the source entry, verbatim.
Classifies the Name that is the modern standard form of a term.
Classifies a Name as a variant form attested in a historical source.
Classifies a Name as an archaic or obsolete form of a term.
